title: 1967 AHSME Problem 27
statement: Two candles of the same length are made of different materials so that one burns out completely at a uniform rate in \(3\) hours and the other in \(4\) hours. At what time P.M. should the candles be lighted so that, at \(4\) P.M., one stub is twice the length of the other?

solutions.text:
After \(t\) hours, the faster and slower candles have fractions \(1-\frac{t}{3}\) and \(1-\frac{t}{4}\) remaining. The slower stub must be twice the faster: \[ 1-\frac t4=2\left(1-\frac t3\right). \] Thus \(t=\frac{12}{5}=2\) hours \(24\) minutes. Counting back from \(4\) P.M. gives \(1{:}36\) P.M.

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Let \(t\) be the number of hours the candles burn before \(4\) P.M.
